# Browser suite contention: `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2` lets two full suites starve each other

Discovered while auditing TCE `CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I` — `discovered-from:CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I`.

## Problem
`run_tests.py` bounds concurrent test runs with `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (default **2**, introduced by `SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG`). Two concurrent full suites — e.g. two `implement.py finish` gates in different TCE worktrees, plus an audit's F3 auto-execution — each spin up a 4-worker Chromium browser stage (`maxWorkers: 4` in `vite.config.ts`). On a single host this oversubscribes CPU/GPU, so timing-sensitive browser tests time out and vitest runs get **SIGKILLed (exit 137)** or **hang (exit 124)**.

## Impact
A repo can go many hours without a green full-suite run, blocking audits/releases and producing misleading `test-failure` items.

**TCE evidence (2026-09-20):** last green full-suite cache entry **~29 h old**; consecutive entries `exit 124 / 137 / 1 / 1`; observed **≥2 concurrent full suites** and **30+ vitest/chromium processes**; load average ~8–12 on 16 cores. `tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` fails 3 animation-timeout tests under load while passing **6/6 in isolation** (10.2 s).

## Expected Behaviour
- Full-suite runs (or at least browser-heavy suites) are serialized per repo/host to **1**.
- `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` becomes context-aware (browser suites ⇒ 1) or the default drops where a Chromium stage is present.
- `implement.py` full-suite gates acquire the guard and log `queued_at` / `wait_seconds` rather than colliding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two full project suites in the same repo never execute their browser stages simultaneously (verified by observing serialized runs / semaphore telemetry).
- [ ] `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (or a browser-stage-specific cap) prevents cross-suite browser starvation; the behaviour is documented.
- [ ] `implement.py` full-suite gates acquire the guard and emit a `queued_at`/`wait_seconds` log line.
- [ ] A TCE full-suite re-run during a multi-agent period yields a green full-suite cache entry.

## Related Work
- `SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG` — Extend test skill to use shared concurrency primitive (the `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` default of 2 this refines).
- `CG-0MUA7RRXL007GEHW` (TCE) — the timing-fragile `upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` surfaced by this contention.
- `CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I` (TCE) — audit blocked on obtaining a green full-suite run.

## Key Files
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` handling.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` / `skill/shared/queue.py` — shared bounded-concurrency primitive.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — the full-suite finish gate.

# Intake Brief: child-audit cascade can recursively execute the full suite (cold cache / concurrent runs)

## Problem Statement

A full-suite run can enter unbounded recursion when the test cache is cold (e.g.
a fresh worktree/commit) and/or another full-suite run is executing
concurrently. An audit test spawns a **real** `audit_runner.py issue` child
subprocess; that child audit's automatic full-suite execution (F3) hits a cache
miss and executes the real pytest suite, which re-runs the same test, which
spawns another real child audit — and so on until the outer timeout (observed
1500s+ and 19–50+ nested processes). The per-run child cap
(`--max-child-audits`) does not bound this because it resets in every child
process.

## Users & User Stories

- **Agent / operator:** "When I run the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full`)
  or `implement.py finish` from a cold cache, it must complete in bounded time
  — no runaway nesting that blows the timeout."
- **Reviewer / producer:** "A child-audit cascade must never re-enter the full
  suite; if it would, it must fail fast with a clear diagnostic rather than
  hanging the release gate."
- **Future maintainer:** "Audit tests that exercise the child-cascade path must
  never spawn a real child audit, and there must be a documented convention and
  a regression test that keeps it that way."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Cold-cache full-suite completion:** `run_tests.py --scope full`
  completes (no recursion) from a **cold** test cache in a fresh
  `implement.py start` worktree. *Verification:* clear the cache / start a fresh
  worktree, run the suite, and confirm a single suite invocation (no nested
  `audit_runner.py issue … --force` → `pytest` chain) with no timeout.
- **AC2 — Recursion guard (bounded, fails fast):** an audit's automatic
  full-suite execution (F3) cannot itself trigger another automatic full-suite
  execution. When a suite run is already owned by an ancestor process, a nested
  audit stands down (or the cascade is depth-capped) and emits a clear
  diagnostic; execution-dependent ACs stay partial/fail-open. *Verification:* a
  dedicated regression test simulates a child-audit cascade with a cold cache
  and asserts no nested suite execution occurs and the run returns promptly.
- **AC3 — Test isolation preserved:** `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` (and any
  other audit test that reaches the child-audit subprocess) mocks the
  child-audit subprocess, so no real `audit_runner.py issue` child is spawned —
  while still asserting its intended behaviour (non-zero rc, plus
  `Failed to persist audit for child …` and `Aborting` on stderr).
  *Verification:* the class's tests pass in isolation and in the full suite; the
  test asserts the (mocked) child invocation rather than real execution.
- **AC4 — Production behaviour preserved:** outside a nested/test suite-run
  context, a standalone audit's F3 automatic full-suite execution is unchanged.
  *Verification:* existing F3 tests remain green, plus a new test proving a
  standalone audit still auto-executes on a cold cache.
- **AC5 — Documentation updated:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and the shared test-writing guidance
  document the recursion guard, the ancestor-ownership rule, and the
  "mock the child-audit subprocess in tests" convention. All related
  documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
  README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC6 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes, both
  sequentially and from a cold cache, with zero new regressions; no test is
  skipped, xfailed, or retried to reach green. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — it is
  managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.)

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken production child-audit behaviour.** A standalone audit must
  keep the F3 auto-execution behaviour; the guard applies only to nested /
  test auto-run contexts.
- **Reuse existing nesting machinery where possible.** Prefer the existing
  ancestor-ownership marker (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`, set by `run_tests.py`
  while it owns the checkout) or an analogous audit-specific marker propagated
  into child-audit subprocesses, rather than new bespoke state.
- **Keep the per-run child cap intact.** `--max-child-audits` /
  `AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_AUDITS` (SA-0MSKB6V5Q007YDHE) remains; the new guard
  addresses cross-process depth, which the per-process cap cannot.
- **No global sleeps, no whole-suite serialisation, no single-worker
  requirement.**
- **Minimal blast radius:** change shared helpers only where required; re-verify
  the full suite if a shared helper changes.
- **Worktree discipline:** implementation happens in the `implement.py start`
  worktree; never push to `main`.

## Existing State

- `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py:631`)
  calls `audit_runner.cmd_issue(..., audit_children=True)` with a faked `wl`
  runner but **no mock of `audit_runner.subprocess.run`**, so the child-audit
  spawn at `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:~10040` runs for real.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` already mocks
  `subprocess.run` (4 sites); `test_audit_runner_core.py` likewise. Other
  `audit_children=True` call sites pass a canned `child_audit_raw` or otherwise
  bypass the spawn, but this must be re-audited during implementation.
- Auto-execution path: `cmd_issue` → `_auto_green_run_outcome` (cache
  classification) → on `_FULL_SUITE_CACHE_MISS` →
  `_run_tests_via_test_skill` (`audit_runner.py:2465`) →
  `run_cached(full_suite_commands(...), force=True)` (`skill/test_cache.py:341`).
  `run_cached` does not go through `run_tests.py`.
- `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:116`,
  `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py:45`) is set by `run_tests.py` while it owns
  the checkout and is inherited by subprocesses; nested `run_tests.py`/pytest
  stand down, but the audit auto-execution path does not consult it.
- The per-run child-audit cap (`AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_AUDITS`, default 5,
  `audit_runner.py:544`) is per-process, so cross-process depth is unbounded.
- Observed evidence: `implement.py finish` timed out after 1500s; a plain
  `run_tests.py --scope full` also timed out (>1500s). The offending test
  passes in isolation (2 passed in 1.44s); the full suite passes sequentially
  on a warm cache (350s, 2743 passed).

## Desired Change

1. Gate the audit's F3 auto-execution on ancestor suite ownership: when a suite
   run is already in progress in an ancestor process (reuse
   `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` or an analogous marker propagated into the
   child-audit command), stand down with a clear diagnostic and leave
   execution-dependent ACs partial (fail-open) instead of executing a nested
   suite.
2. Mock the child-audit subprocess in `TestChildPersistFailureFatal._run_with_child`
   (and re-audit every `cmd_issue(audit_children=True)` test site), preserving
   the class's persist-failure assertions.
3. Add a regression test proving a child-audit cascade cannot re-enter the full
   suite (bounded, fast fail).
4. Document the guard and the test-mocking convention.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Gate the F3 cache-miss auto-execution
  branch (~L8044-8070) on ancestor suite ownership; propagate the marker into
  the child-audit command (~L10002-10045).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` — Mock
  `audit_runner.subprocess.run` in `TestChildPersistFailureFatal._run_with_child`
  (L631-790); keep the persist-failure assertions.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` — Reference pattern for
  mocking `subprocess.run`; add/adjust the cascade-bounded regression test.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` definition/usage
  (L116, ~L1774); confirm/extend semantics if reused.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — `MARKER_ENV` definition (L45) if the
  marker is shared.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `run_cached(force=True)` (L341) if the guard is
  centralised there rather than in `audit_runner`.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — Document the guard and the
  test-mocking convention.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** the runaway loop is the real child-audit `subprocess.run`
  (`audit_runner.py:~10040`), which resolves `full_suite_commands()` against the
  repository cwd and force-executes on a cold cache. The parent audit's own
  auto-execution resolves against the patched temp target root (no suite), so
  mocking the child spawn plus adding the guard breaks the chain.
- **Assumption:** production dispatch never runs a standalone audit nested
  inside `run_tests.py`, so the ancestor-ownership guard has no effect on
  production audit behaviour (AC4).
- **Risk:** reusing `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` could suppress legitimate
  auto-execution if the marker leaks across processes; mitigate by setting and
  clearing it in a `finally`, as `run_tests.py` already does.
- **Risk:** the guard makes execution-dependent ACs partial for nested audits;
  this is fail-open (never a degraded "met" verdict) and acceptable.
- **Risk:** other tests may still spawn real child audits that only surface
  under a cold cache; mitigate by re-auditing every
  `cmd_issue(audit_children=True)` call site (AC3).
- **Risk (scope creep):** the concurrency-semaphore bypass is a distinct
  defect; recorded as discovered-from SA-0MUJK94QN0015925 rather than folded
  into this item.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MSKB6V5Q007YDHE** (completed) — opt-in child audit cascade with a
  per-run cap; the cap is per-process and does not bound cross-process depth.
- **SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP** (F3 auto-execution hatch) — introduced automatic
  suite execution on a cache miss; this item must bound it without weakening
  the standalone case.
- **SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W** (completed) — automatic read-only full-suite
  verification (cache consumption).
- **SA-0MSJELSWS002UF60** (completed) — `--run-tests` execution; noted that
  child audits are intended to reuse the parent's refreshed cache.
- **SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG** (completed) — test-run concurrency bounding
  (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`); the audit's direct `run_cached` bypasses it.
- **SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63** — sibling test-isolation / recursion-marker work
  (live-repo guard).
- **SA-0MUJK94QN0015925** (discovered-from, new) — audit F3 auto-execution
  bypasses the test concurrency semaphore; out of scope here.
- **discovered-from:SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9** — the find-related v3 review during
  which this defect was found.
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** (completed) — audit staleness race (adjacent audit
  freshness/staleness behaviour).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** – Audit staleness race: post-persist comment bumps updatedAt past auditedAt — passed audits show stale icon (completed)
- **SA-0MRMCK0C8008ESE0** – [test-failure] test_audit_skill_doc.py::TestAuditSkillWorkItemIdDetection::test_scan_match_branch_structure — failing test (completed)
- **SA-0MSHZ08PO009933Y** – Verify full test suite green (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 1500s, aborting, aborts, acceptance, add (+125 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 1500s, aborts, acceptance, add, also (+118 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: aborts, acceptance, add, also, another (+102 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Is an interactive intake interview required, or is the seed context
  sufficient? — Answer (agent): The seed context (problem, process-tree
  evidence, root-cause hypothesis, proposed fix, ACs) was sufficient to draft a
  clear brief; no interactive interview was held. The item was nonetheless on
  stage `idea` and its description was not in canonical brief form, so the full
  intake path was used. Source: work-item inspection (`wl show … --json`).
- Q: What is the scope of the recursion guard — test-context only, or
  nested-run ownership? — Answer (agent, **OPEN QUESTION** with recommended
  option): Reuse ancestor-suite ownership (the existing `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`
  marker or an analogous audit marker propagated to child audits) so an audit
  auto-execution nested inside an outer suite run stands down while standalone
  production audits keep F3 behaviour. **Recommended:** nested-run ownership —
  smallest change that bounds the cascade while satisfying the
  "do not weaken production" constraint. Source: `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:116`,
  `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py:45`. Deferred to plan/implement for final
  mechanism selection; AC4 guards the production-behaviour intent.
- Q: Should the concurrency-semaphore bypass of the audit's `run_cached` path
  be fixed in this item? — Answer (agent): No — filed as
  discovered-from **SA-0MUJK94QN0015925** to keep this item focused on the
  recursion guard. Source: `skill/test_cache.py:341`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:1148`.
- Q: Do other audit tests besides `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` spawn real
  child audits? — Answer (agent): `test_audit_runner_children.py` and
  `test_audit_runner_core.py` already mock `subprocess.run`;
  `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` is the confirmed offender; the remaining
  `audit_children=True` call sites pass a canned `child_audit_raw` or otherwise
  bypass the spawn. Implementation must still re-audit every
  `cmd_issue(audit_children=True)` site. Source: grep across `skill/audit/tests/`.
- Q: Priority — keep `high` or raise to `critical`? — Answer (agent): Keep
  `high`. The defect intermittently blocks the release/test gate (cold cache /
  concurrent runs) but is not a security or data-loss issue and does not always
  break the build. Source: priority classification guide.

## Problem statement

The audit runner's automatic full-suite execution path (F3, SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP) calls run_cached(..., force=True) from skill/test_cache.py directly instead of going through skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py. run_cached does not acquire the shared test semaphore (TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY / TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT) that run_tests.py uses (SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG). Nested audit-triggered suite executions are therefore not bounded host-wide, which compounds the cold-cache/concurrent-run recursion in SA-0MUG47DYG006TV40.

## Evidence

- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py _run_tests_via_test_skill (~L2465-2520) imports run_cached from test_cache (L141) and calls run_cached(command, cwd, force=True, ...).
- skill/test_cache.py run_cached (L341) has no semaphore acquisition; only run_tests.py _test_concurrency_slot (skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py ~L1148) uses the shared test semaphore.
- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG's goal assumed the audit F3 path goes through run_tests.py; it does not.

## Desired change

Route the audit automatic suite execution through the same bounded concurrency primitive as run_tests.py (or acquire the shared test semaphore around run_cached), so audit-triggered executions cannot saturate the host or nest unbounded.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit F3 auto-execution respects TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY / TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT (or documents and enforces an equivalent bound)
- [ ] Regression test proves a nested/parallel audit-triggered execution waits for or fails to acquire the slot rather than running unbounded
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes

# Ship skill: let a release-ready parent override (or absorb) `needsProducerReview` on its children

## Problem statement

The ship release close step (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) skips every item with `needsProducerReview === true`:

```js
const toClose = items.filter((item) => item.needsProducerReview === false);
```

For a **child** item flagged `needsProducerReview=true`, this leaves the child in `in_review`; because `wl close --force` is then refused (to avoid sweeping a non-candidate descendant), the **parent** is refused too and remains un-closed in tracking even though the code has shipped.

### Motivating case (ContextHub v1.0.16)

- Parent `WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28` (`in_review`, audit passed, code on `main`) has 5 children.
- 4 children were closed; the 5th, `WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME`, is `in_review` with `needsProducerReview=true`.
- Result: the parent cannot be closed and remains `in_review` despite shipping. Every other blocker was resolved.

The existing scoping rules (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H) already say a child's audit/review is **covered by an audit-ready `in_review` parent** — so a covered child's `needsProducerReview` flag should not outlive, nor contradict, that parent's ready-to-release determination.

## Users

- **Release manager / release agent:** wants a release-ready parent to be closeable without being blocked by a covered child's stale `needsProducerReview` flag; the release record should reflect what actually shipped.
- **Producer:** must keep a real veto — if a child genuinely needs producer attention, the flag must escalate up and block the release rather than be silently cleared.
- **Auditor / future agent:** needs every flag mutation to be logged with the authorising parent/audit so the override is auditable.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when a child is covered by an audit-ready `in_review` parent, I want its `needsProducerReview` flag cleared (with an explanatory comment) and the child closed, so the parent can be closed after release.
- As a producer, when a child that genuinely needs my attention would otherwise be swept, I want the parent flagged `needsProducerReview=true` with the child id(s) enumerated, so the release is blocked until I approve.
- As an operator running `--dry-run`, I want the planned overrides/escalations reported with no worklog mutations.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A child with `needsProducerReview=true` under an audit-ready `in_review` parent is closed after its flag is cleared, with an explanatory comment on the child.
2. A child that genuinely needs attention causes the parent to be flagged `needsProducerReview=true` with a comment naming the child(ren); the parent then fails the producer-review gate.
3. Clearing a child flag is refused when the parent is not `in_review` or its audit is not `readyToClose`.
4. `--dry-run` performs no mutations and reports the intended child overrides and parent escalations.
5. Unit tests inject `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn`/`runCloseCommand` boundaries and never mutate the live worklog.
6. `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and `SKILL.md` document the override/escalation contract.
7. `npm run build` and existing suites pass.

## Desired change

When the release skill evaluates a **child** with `needsProducerReview=true`, it must resolve the flag against the parent's readiness:

1. **Parent overrides (default when the parent is release-ready):** if the child's nearest `in_review` ancestor is an audit-ready release candidate (`readyToClose === true`), the skill may **clear the child's `needsProducerReview` flag** (set `false`) and record a comment on the child explaining the override, then close it. The parent's passing audit is what authorises the override.
2. **Genuine attention required:** if the child genuinely needs producer attention (unresolved question, ambiguous requirement, manual approval owed), the skill must **escalate to the parent** instead: set `needsProducerReview=true` on the parent and add a comment **enumerating the child id(s)** that require attention. The parent then blocks the release through the existing producer-review gate (Step 3.6) — the correct fail-safe.
3. The override must **never** be authorised by status alone: it requires the parent's passing audit (`readyToClose === true`). A non-`in_review` parent or an unaudited parent must not silently clear a child flag.
4. Every flag change (child cleared, or parent escalated) must be **logged** with a comment naming the authorising parent/audit or the children that need attention.
5. `--dry-run` must report the planned overrides/escalations without mutating any work item.

## Existing state

- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` (`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) filters candidates to `needsProducerReview === false`, then refuses any candidate whose `--force` close would sweep descendants outside the candidate set (`candidateIds`), reporting them as `refusedItems` (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H AC9/AC10). This is the mechanism that leaves a parent un-closed when a child is skipped.
- `getCandidateItems()` (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`) projects only `{id, title, needsProducerReview, parentId}` from `wl list --stage in_review` — it does not carry audit state.
- The producer-review gate (Step 3.6, `checkProducerReviewStatus`) is scoped to **top-level** candidates via `getTopLevelCandidateItems()`; children never block it.
- The final-validation sweep (Step 3.7, `check-final-validation.js`) already resolves child scope: a child whose nearest `in_review` ancestor has a passing audit (`readyToClose === true`) is `covered` and skipped; a child with no audit-ready `in_review` ancestor is `uncovered` and blocks if it has a missing/stale/failing audit or `needsProducerReview === true`. It can inject `getItemsFn`, `runAuditShow`, `runAuditCommand`, `resolveAuditRunnerFn`.
- The close step runs **after** the release has merged (Step 11, gated by `verifyReleaseMerge()`); Steps 3.6/3.7 run **before** the merge.

## Constraints

- The override must be authorised only by an audit-ready `in_review` parent (`readyToClose === true`); never by status alone.
- `--dry-run` must remain mutation-free.
- Unit tests must be hermetic (no live `wl`/audit-runner calls, no live worklog mutation).
- Changes are confined to the ship skill (`skill/ship/scripts/`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md`) and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.
- Preserve existing behaviour for top-level items and for genuinely-flagged uncovered children.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()`: add child-flag resolution (override vs escalate), comments, and `--dry-run` reporting; pass through new injectable boundaries.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — possibly extend `getCandidateItems()` projection (e.g. carry `parentId` already present) and/or add an ancestor/audit resolver used by the close step.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — likely the pre-ship home of the escalation half of the contract (see Open Question 1).
- `skill/ship/tests/` — new hermetic unit tests for override, escalation, refusal, and `--dry-run` (there is currently only `test_discord_notify.mjs`).
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — document the override/escalation contract and close-step behaviour.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — document the override/escalation contract.

## Risks and assumptions

- **R1 — Escalation timing:** if escalation (case 2) runs only in the post-ship close step, setting `needsProducerReview=true` on the parent cannot block *this* release (Steps 3.6/3.7 have already passed). It would only affect the next release. Resolving this is Open Question 1.
- **R2 — Missing audit data in the close step:** the close step's candidate projection has no `readyToClose`, so it cannot currently authorise an override. A new injectable boundary is likely required (Open Question 2); AC5's stated boundary list may be incomplete.
- **R3 — Overriding a producer's explicit signal:** clearing `needsProducerReview=true` mutates a human-set signal. The contract relies on the parent's passing audit as the authorising evidence and on a mandatory comment for traceability (Open Question 3).
- **R4 — Scope creep:** additional improvements (e.g. a general ancestor-audit cache, change to the Step 3.6/3.7 ordering) are recorded as separate work items, not folded into this one.
- **Assumption:** the "nearest `in_review` ancestor" walk semantics match the existing final-validation coverage walk (skip non-`in_review` / non-passing ancestors, continue up the chain, break cycles conservatively).

## Related work

- SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H — parent-coverage / out-of-scope child rules for child audits in the final-validation gate (completed, `in_review`).
- SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP — close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done` (open). Complementary: that item stops refusing on already-done descendants; this item resolves the `needsProducerReview` child case.
- SA-0MS21B5MP004AUUS — close work items after release only when `readyToClose` and producerReview conditions are met (completed). Origin of the producer-review gating and the close-step filter.
- SA-0MS4TXDPG003OFYO — filter `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` by `needsProducerReview` (completed). The behaviour being refined.
- SA-0MS4TJR2R0043UHO — extend `getCandidateItems` and add `checkProducerReviewStatus` (completed).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSKB6WA8009XKTX** – Audit: refresh measured baseline and performance docs (completed)
- **SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E** – [CRITICAL] Audit runner has circular dependency — child audit verdict blocks parent regardless of stage (completed)
- **SA-0MLQ8YP2X0I2XJ0M** – Prerequisite Validation and Error Handling (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched on the terms shared with this brief package (audit, ancestor, approval, child, close, producer, ready, …).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched on the terms shared with this brief package (acceptance, ancestor, child, producer, ready, …).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched on the terms shared with this brief package (ambiguous, ancestor, child, needsproducerreview, producer, …).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — Where does the child→parent **escalation** (contract case 2) execute? (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790506262-3754936-23077`)
- **Context:** The close step (Step 11) runs *after* the release has merged; the producer-review gate (Step 3.6) and final-validation sweep (Step 3.7) run *before*. The brief says setting `needsProducerReview=true` on the parent makes it "fail the producer-review gate", which is impossible if performed at close time for the current release.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** implement escalation in the **pre-ship final-validation sweep (Step 3.7)**: when an *uncovered* child has `needsProducerReview=true` and no audit-ready `in_review` ancestor, set the flag on the nearest `in_review` ancestor (or top-level parent) with a comment enumerating the child(ren), so the gate blocks *before* shipping. The close step then only performs overrides for covered children.
- **Alternative A:** implement everything in the post-ship close step; escalation only affects the *next* release (does not fail the current producer-review gate).
- **Alternative B:** both — escalate pre-ship in Step 3.7 and re-assert in the close step.
- **Answer:** _OPEN — pending producer decision._

### Q2 (OPEN QUESTION) — How does the close step learn an ancestor's `readyToClose` (and is AC5's boundary list complete)? (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790506262-3754936-23077`)
- **Context:** `getCandidateItems()` projects only `{id, title, needsProducerReview, parentId}` — no audit state. AC5 names only `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn`/`runCloseCommand` as injectable boundaries, which is insufficient to resolve an ancestor's audit without a live call.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** add an injectable boundary (e.g. `getAncestorStatusFn` / `getParentAuditFn`) that resolves the nearest `in_review` ancestor and its audit verdict, defaulting to a `wl show` + `wl audit-show` query; extend AC5 accordingly. Keeps tests hermetic.
- **Alternative A:** derive a parent map from `getCandidateItemsFn()` alone — insufficient, because a non-candidate/unaudited ancestor is not present in the candidate list.
- **Answer:** _OPEN — pending producer decision._

### Q3 (OPEN QUESTION) — Is clearing a producer-set flag authorised by the parent's passing audit alone, or does it need an explicit opt-in? (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790506262-3754936-23077`)
- **Context:** `needsProducerReview=true` is a human/producer signal. Desired-behaviour item 3 says the parent's `readyToClose === true` audit is the authorisation; desired-behaviour item 4 requires a comment. AC3 only forbids authorising by status alone.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** override is authorised solely by the parent's passing audit (`readyToClose === true`) plus a mandatory explanatory comment naming the authorising parent/audit id — matching desired behaviour items 3 and 4 as written.
- **Alternative A:** require an explicit release-command opt-in (e.g. `--override-child-producer-review`) before any child flag may be cleared.
- **Answer:** _OPEN — pending producer decision._

## Problem

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` calls `test_cache.run_cached(...)` directly (e.g. `_run_changed_scope_pytest` ~L2026, and `run_tests` ~L2117/2142/2155/2182/2222) to satisfy the finish gate. `run_cached` does NOT acquire the host-wide test semaphore; only `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` does. Every `implement.py finish` therefore executes suites outside the pacing semaphore, contributing to oversubscription.

## Decision (producer, SA-0MUJL211C008GHMZ)

The **test skill** owns routing all test executions through the pacer (Q2 = test skill). This item must make `implement.py` acquire the same host-wide `"test"` semaphore that `run_tests.py` uses (namespace `test`, `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`/`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`), or delegate execution to the test-skill runner, so no implement-gate suite runs unpaced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Every real suite execution triggered by `implement.py` (changed-scope and full-scope) acquires the host-wide `"test"` semaphore before spawning, matching `run_tests.py` namespace/semantics.
- AC2: Cache hits do not consume a semaphore slot (parity with `run_tests.py`).
- AC3: The pacer is honoured for implement-gate runs; bounded wait via `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` with clear actionable logging on timeout.
- AC4: Tests cover (a) a paced implement-gate run and (b) the cache-hit no-slot path; no direct unguarded `run_cached` execution path remains in `implement.py`.
- AC5: Docs updated; JSON output continues to be produced.

## Constraints

- Keep env-var mechanism only (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`/`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`); no new config file (producer Q3 = env for now).
- Do not depend on or duplicate the audit semaphore.
